methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures that each unit can be individually assessed for coverage and similarity.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Build an XOR gate using an assign statement (output out_assign).
Build an XOR gate using a combinational always block (output out_always_comb).
Build an XOR gate using a clocked always block (output out_always_ff).
The clocked always block produces a different circuit from the other two.
The clocked always block infers a flip-flop.
The flip-flop introduces a one-clock-cycle delay in the output.
Module has inputs clk, a, and b.
Module has outputs out_assign, out_always_comb, and out_always_ff.
spec_atomic_units: Module has inputs clk, a, and b.
Module has outputs out_assign, out_always_comb, and out_always_ff.
out_assign implements XOR using assign statement.
out_always_comb implements XOR using combinational always block.
out_always_ff implements XOR using clocked always block.
out_assign changes immediately when a or b changes.
out_always_comb changes immediately when a or b changes.
out_always_ff changes only at the positive edge of clk.
out_always_ff's new value is the XOR of a and b at that clock edge.
Clocked always block introduces a one-clock-cycle delay.
Critical path for out_assign and out_always_comb is the propagation delay through the XOR gate.
Critical path for out_always_ff includes setup time, clock-to-output delay of the flip-flop.
Registers out_always_comb and out_always_ff are declared using reg.
The clocked `always` block introduces a one-clock-cycle delay due to the inferred flip-flop.
